guard: x54-arg-scanner: the argument scanner carries no per-token cost that scales with a cap-legal command
guard_site: lib/templates.py, the dependency-gate argument scanner - `_pkg_name`/`_PKGNAME`, the `_APPSET` membership test, and the `_bbuf` two-level append. NAMED, NOT NUMBERED: line numbers into the emitted artifact drift with every comment edit and two earlier rounds of this class got them wrong in OPPOSITE directions.
why: THREE per-token costs shared one loop, and only two of them were ever named
in the queue row. The third - `is_approved` scanning the project's whole
approved list per token, with no early exit on a miss - scales with a
variable the PROJECT sets in deps.md, so it was invisible to a fixture that
approves one package. Measured with the other two fixed: 5.4 s at K=1,
13.0 s at K=60, 31.9 s at K=200, against a 60 s ceiling that fails OPEN.
TWO ROWS ARE NEEDED AND NEITHER IS REDUNDANT, which is the whole reason
this set exists rather than a single behavioural check:
* row 6 runs at 800 approved packages and reads an rc. It is the ONLY
thing that sees the `is_approved` revert (115 s -> cancelled).
* row 7 is a RATIO against a no-head control at the same byte count. It
is the only thing that sees the fork and the append, because MEASURED
those reverts leave 43.3 s and 26.2 s - inside the ceiling, so rc 2, so
every rc-based row stays green. Neither scales with K and token count is
capped by `_CMD_MAXLEN`, so no cap-legal payload makes them cross alone.
TWO OF THE FIVE BYPASSES LEAVE THE SOURCE SHAPE ENTIRELY PLAUSIBLE.
`flush-every-iteration` and `window-unbounded` change one threshold and keep
the two-level buffer, its variable names and its comment byte-identical. A
source-text pin passes both. That is the class this gate exists for, and
this repo has already shipped it twice.
A PASS HERE MEANS THE FIVE EDITS BELOW ARE CAUGHT. It is not a closure
proof: the enumeration is bounded by review, not by this file.

mutations.why: Put the subshell fork back, per package token. NOT a naive text-revert: `pkg_name` no longer exists, so restoring the old call would be an unbound-command crash rather than a bypass, and the gate correctly scores a crashed cell as evidence of nothing. This wraps the surviving `_pkg_name` in a command substitution instead - a plausible refactor, and it runs. MEASURED 43.3 s vs a 4.4 s control = 9.83x.

Put the O(K) linear scan back in place of the set lookup. INVISIBLE to the ratio row (1.18x) because at one approved package a scan and a lookup are indistinguishable - which is exactly why row 6 installs an 800-package fixture. MEASURED 115.5 s there, i.e. cancelled at the ceiling.
Put the growing-string append back. The trailing flush below the loop then appends an empty `_bbuf` and is harmless, so this runs and is O(n^2) again. MEASURED 26.2 s = 6.07x.

DEFEATS THE BOUND WHILE LEAVING EVERY SOURCE STRING PLAUSIBLE. The two-level buffer, its names and its comment stay byte-identical; only the threshold moves to 0, so the buffer flushes on every token and `blocked="$blocked$_bbuf"` is a growing-string append again. A source-text pin cannot tell this from the fix. MEASURED 25.9 s = 6.04x.

The same threshold in the opposite direction: a window nothing reaches, so the flush never runs inside the loop and `_bbuf` itself becomes the unbounded growing string. Also leaves every pinned string intact. MEASURED 27.1 s = 6.30x.

NEGATIVE CONTROL. A one-word spelling change in a COMMENT inside the same emitted body. It moves the golden digests - which is what digest_suites is for - and must ESCAPE every behavioural suite. If this is ever reported CAUGHT, the suites are red for any edit and every row above is meaningless.
